source_evidence.observation: The underlying problem is the overdetermined least-squares problem min_x ||Ax-b||_2 with A in R^(m x n), b in R^m, and m > n.

The paper assumes throughout that A and SA have full column rank. It defines normwise least-squares backward error through perturbations for which the candidate is an exact minimizer of the perturbed residual, measured by the Frobenius norm of the concatenated data perturbation.

SAA Blendenpik draws S in R^(s x m), computes B=SA, obtains the triangular R factor using Householder QR, explicitly computes Y=AR^(-1) by forward substitution, applies unpreconditioned LSQR to Yz=b, and computes x=R^(-1)z by back substitution.
Computations use precision u. The standard multiplication model uses gamma_n = n u/(1-n u), with entrywise absolute-value bounds; the induced matrix bound uses the spectral norm.

A computed back-substitution result satisfies (R_hat+DeltaR_hat)x_hat=b with ||DeltaR_hat||_2 <= gamma_n sqrt(n)||R_hat||_2. The same page defines tilde_gamma_(m n)=c m n u/(1-c m n u) for a small integer constant c in the Householder QR model.

The computed preconditioned matrix is Y_hat=A R_hat^(-1)+DeltaY_form, where DeltaY_form is the forward-substitution formation error. The exact constants are C1=sqrt(s n) gamma_m+sqrt(n) tilde_gamma_(s n)(1+sqrt(s n) gamma_m) and k(S)=||S||_2||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2.

The inherited setup has A in R^(m x n) with linearly independent columns, S in R^(s x m) with linearly independent rows, m>s>n, and exact economy QR factorizations A=Q_A R_A and SA=QR. The numerical assumptions are kappa_2(S Q_A)<49, n^2 u<1/201, m/n+sqrt(n)>200, and kappa_2(A)<1/(3 C1 k(S)).

The theorem assumes an LSQR iterate z_hat satisfying z_hat=(Y_hat+DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b+delta_b). The proof constructs DeltaA=(Y_hat R_hat-A)+DeltaY_hat R_hat+Y_hat DeltaR_hat+DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat, gives the rowwise formation relation, and derives the immediate spectral-norm composition estimate.

source_evidence.anchor: completion of the proof of Theorem 3.5 and following interpretation
source_evidence.observation: The proof obtains ||DeltaA||_2 <= 2||S||_2||A||_2(3.02 n gamma_n||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2+1.005||DeltaY_hat||_2), using n+sqrt(n)<=2n and sqrt(n)gamma_n<=n gamma_n<=1/200. The following paragraph makes backward stability conditional on both ||DeltaY_hat||_2 and ||delta_b||_2/||b||_2 being O(u).

binders: Explicitly in Theorem 3.5, S is an embedding matrix in R^(s x m) and A is in R^(m x n); the inherited Theorem 3.4 setup has integer dimensions m>s>n, A with linearly independent columns, and S with linearly independent rows. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
The right-hand side is b in R^m, and the sought and computed solution vectors lie in R^n. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 905, equation (1.1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3.)
Q_A and R_A are defined by the exact economy QR factorization A=Q_A R_A; Q and R are defined by the exact economy QR factorization SA=QR. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4.)

R_hat is the computed triangular factor, Y_hat is the explicitly formed computed matrix approximating A R_hat^(-1), z_hat is the terminating LSQR iterate, and x_hat is the final computed back-substitution result. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5 and proof.)

After S and A satisfy the inherited assumptions and the algorithm produces Y_hat and z_hat, equation (3.9) assumes perturbation witnesses DeltaY_hat and delta_b; the proof then obtains a back-substitution witness DeltaR_hat and constructs DeltaA. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, equation (3.9) and proof.)
hypotheses: The inherited exact-factorization setup is A=Q_A R_A and SA=QR, with A full column rank, S full row rank, and m>s>n. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4.)
The numerical inequalities are kappa_2(S Q_A)<49, n^2 u<1/201, m/n+sqrt(n)>200, and kappa_2(A)<1/(3 C1 k(S)). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equations (3.6) and (3.7).)

Algorithm 1.3 is applied: Householder QR produces R_hat, forward substitution explicitly forms Y_hat, LSQR is unpreconditioned, and the final mapping from z_hat to x_hat is performed by back substitution. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, section 3.4.)

The terminal LSQR iterate must admit witnesses satisfying z_hat=(Y_hat+DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b+delta_b). No magnitude bound on either witness is included in this hypothesis. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, equation (3.9).)

The section excludes a sketch-and-solve initialization and bases the result only on the terminal backward-error property, allowing stability analysis from any starting point. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, opening of section 3.4.)
conclusions: The theorem text states that the computed x_hat has a perturbed-data relation (A+DeltaA)x_hat=b+delta_b. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
The proof derives the exact least-squares identity x_hat=(A+DeltaA)^dagger(b+delta_b). (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, proof of Theorem 3.5.)
The constructed matrix perturbation is exactly DeltaA=(Y_hat R_hat-A)+DeltaY_hat R_hat+Y_hat DeltaR_hat+DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, proof of Theorem 3.5.)

For every row i, the formation error satisfies y_hat_i^T R_hat-a_i^T=-y_hat_i^T Delta_i R_hat with the entrywise bound |Delta_i R_hat|<=gamma_n|R_hat|. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, rowwise formation-error display.)
Consequently, ||Y_hat R_hat-A||_2<=n gamma_n||R_hat||_2||Y_hat||_2. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, line following the rowwise display.)

Before substituting global bounds, the exact composition estimate is ||DeltaA||_2<=||R_hat||_2((n+sqrt(n))gamma_n||Y_hat||_2+(1+sqrt(n)gamma_n)||DeltaY_hat||_2). (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, immediate compositional estimate.)
The proof bounds ||R_hat||_2<2||S||_2||A||_2 and ||Y_hat||_2<1.51||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2 under the inherited assumptions. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, final two displays.)
The stated final bound is ||DeltaA||_2<||S||_2||A||_2(6.04 n gamma_n||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2+2.01||DeltaY_hat||_2). (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)

The paper's subsequent O(u) backward-stability interpretation is conditional: it additionally requires ||DeltaY_hat||_2=O(u) and ||delta_b||_2/||b||_2=O(u). (PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, paragraph following Theorem 3.5.)
definitions_and_conventions: The base problem is the least-squares minimization min_x ||Ax-b||_2, not an assumed consistent square linear system. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 905, equation (1.1).)

The paper's normwise least-squares backward error asks for perturbations under which x is an exact minimizer of the perturbed residual and measures the concatenated perturbation [DeltaA,Delta b] in Frobenius norm. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, equation (1.2).)
A superscript dagger denotes the matrix pseudoinverse. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, footnote 3.)

DeltaY_form:=Y_hat-A R_hat^(-1) is the numerical error from explicitly forming the preconditioned matrix by forward substitution. It is distinct from the LSQR backward perturbation DeltaY_hat in equation (3.9). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, footnote 5.)

The proof uses phi(R_hat)=n gamma_n kappa_2(R_hat)/(1-sqrt(n)gamma_n kappa_2(R_hat)) when bounding the formation error and ||Y_hat||_2. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equation (3.5); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, final display.)
Hats denote quantities for which floating-point rounding errors are being accounted for. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 916, opening of section 3.)
implicit_context: The paper's standing convention is that A and SA have full column rank, so the original least-squares solution and the sketch-derived triangular inverse are well-defined. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, standing full-rank convention.)

Although Algorithm 1.3 draws a random sketch, Theorem 3.5 is a deterministic implication conditional on the realized S and A satisfying the stated inequalities; the theorem itself contains no probability level. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)

The paper does not prove that LSQR on Y_hat supplies small perturbations; it explicitly says that backward stability of LSQR on a well-conditioned matrix depends on the precise implementation and lacks a cited definitive theorem. (PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, discussion following Theorem 3.5.)
statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract is specifically for SAA Blendenpik, Algorithm 1.3: sketch A, compute the Householder-QR triangular factor R_hat, explicitly form Y_hat=A R_hat^(-1) by forward substitution, run LSQR on Y_hat z=b with no preconditioner, and recover x_hat by a single back substitution with R_hat. The proof does not describe sketch-and-precondition LSQR or repeated applications of R_hat^(-1). (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, section 3.4.)
numerical_model: Computations use a precision u much smaller than one, with arithmetic modeled as exact up to that precision. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, opening of section 2.3.)
The standard rounding constant is gamma_n=n u/(1-n u), rather than the first-order replacement n u. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, equation (2.1).)

Householder QR uses tilde_gamma_(m n)=c m n u/(1-c m n u) for a small integer c; C1 uses the specialization tilde_gamma_(s n). (PDF p. 11, printed p. 915, Householder QR model; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, equation (3.4).)

The final back substitution is represented by (R_hat+DeltaR_hat)x_hat=z_hat with ||DeltaR_hat||_2<=gamma_n sqrt(n)||R_hat||_2. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 915, equation (2.6); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, proof of Theorem 3.5.)
Forward-substitution formation errors are represented row by row by an entrywise perturbation bounded by gamma_n|R_hat|. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, rowwise formation-error display.)
error_notions: DeltaY_form is a forward numerical formation error, DeltaY_hat and delta_b are LSQR backward-error witnesses, DeltaR_hat is a triangular-solve backward error, and DeltaA is the composed perturbation to the original matrix. These roles are not interchangeable. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, Lemma 3.2; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, equation (3.9), proof, and footnote 5.)
The theorem quantitatively bounds only ||DeltaA||_2. It supplies no theorem-level bound on ||delta_b||_2 or ||DeltaY_hat||_2. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
The proof establishes that x_hat is an exact least-squares solution for the perturbed data through a pseudoinverse identity. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, proof of Theorem 3.5.)

The claim of overall backward stability is interpretive and conditional on the LSQR perturbations being O(u), including relative right-hand-side error ||delta_b||_2/||b||_2. (PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, discussion following Theorem 3.5.)
norms: For vectors, ||.||_2 is the Euclidean norm; for matrices in the theorem and proof, ||.||_2 is the spectral norm. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, discussion after equation (2.2); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)

The paper's general backward-error definition uses the Frobenius norm ||[DeltaA,Delta b]||_F, whereas Theorem 3.5 supplies a spectral-norm bound for DeltaA alone. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, equation (1.2); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
Absolute-value bars around matrices in the rounding relations denote entrywise absolute value. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, equation (2.1); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, rowwise formation bound.)

kappa_2 is the spectral condition number, and ||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2 is the spectral norm of the pseudoinverse. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, condition-number definition; PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, equation (3.4).)
constants_and_indexing: The dimensions obey m>s>n; S is s by m, A and Y_hat are m by n, R_hat is n by n, and b is length m. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 905, equation (1.1); PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4.)
C1 is exactly sqrt(s n)gamma_m+sqrt(n)tilde_gamma_(s n)(1+sqrt(s n)gamma_m), and k(S) is exactly ||S||_2||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, equation (3.4).)
The inherited fixed thresholds are 49, 1/201, 200, and the factor 3 in kappa_2(A)<1/(3 C1 k(S)). (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equations (3.6) and (3.7).)

The rowwise relation applies to every row i of A and Y_hat; the related substitution setup indexes rows from 1 through m. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 915, discussion preceding equation (2.5); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, rowwise formation-error display.)

The immediate estimate retains n+sqrt(n) and 1+sqrt(n)gamma_n. The final constants arise using n+sqrt(n)<=2n and sqrt(n)gamma_n<=1/200, yielding 3.02 and 1.005 before the outer factor 2, and 6.04 and 2.01 in the theorem statement. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, compositional estimate and theorem; PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, completion of proof.)
higher_order_terms: The exact definition of DeltaA retains the product DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat; the paper does not discard it as a second-order term. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, exact DeltaA definition.)
The factor 1+sqrt(n)gamma_n multiplying ||DeltaY_hat||_2 retains the contribution of that cross term. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, immediate compositional estimate.)
gamma_n is retained as n u/(1-n u), so its denominator is not omitted in the formal bound. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, equation (2.1).)

C1 has an exact definition in equation (3.4); its later O((sqrt(s n)m+s n^(3/2))u) description is explanatory and does not replace that definition in assumption (3.7). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 917, equation (3.4); PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4.)

The theorem's matrix perturbation bound has explicit constants and no O(u) remainder. O(u) appears only in the subsequent conditional interpretation of LSQR backward stability. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5; PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, following discussion.)
exceptional_values: The inherited rank and conditioning assumptions ensure that the required triangular factors and pseudoinverses are well-defined; equation (2.6) itself is stated for a nonsingular upper-triangular matrix. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 915, section 2.3.3; PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, Theorem 3.4.)

The inequality n^2 u<1/201 implies the proof's n gamma_n<=1/200 estimate and keeps the relevant gamma denominators away from zero. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equation (3.6); PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, completion of proof.)

No nonzero assumption on b is stated. Consequently, the formal theorem remains meaningful at b=0, but the later ratio ||delta_b||_2/||b||_2 is undefined there. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 905, equation (1.1); PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, following discussion.)
The cited numerical model does not explicitly discuss overflow, underflow, subnormal values, NaNs, or infinities. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, opening of section 2.3 and equation (2.1).)

undebatable_constraints: The result concerns the sketch-and-apply algorithm with explicitly formed Y_hat and unpreconditioned LSQR, followed by one back substitution. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3.)
The numerical assumptions from equations (3.6) and (3.7) must be retained with their exact constants and strict inequalities. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equations (3.6) and (3.7).)
Equation (3.9) is a hypothesis on the terminal LSQR iterate, not a conclusion proved about LSQR. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
DeltaY_hat in equation (3.9) must not be identified with the forward-substitution formation error DeltaY_form. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, footnote 5.)
The same right-hand-side perturbation delta_b from equation (3.9) is carried into the perturbed original problem. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, equation (3.9) and proof.)
The exact four-term DeltaA formula, including DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat, must be preserved. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, proof of Theorem 3.5.)
The rowwise entrywise bound and the resulting n gamma_n spectral bound are both explicit parts of the derivation. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, rowwise formation-error display and following line.)
The final matrix bound is spectral-norm and uses 6.04 n gamma_n and 2.01 exactly; it is not merely an unspecified O(u) result. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)

No quantitative bound on delta_b or DeltaY_hat may be added to the formal theorem; their O(u) size appears only as a later condition for interpreting the algorithm as backward stable. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5; PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, following discussion.)

The theorem is conditional and deterministic once S is fixed; no probability statement or sketch distribution is part of Theorem 3.5. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)

ambiguities.issue: The theorem statement writes the literal equation (A+DeltaA)x_hat=b+delta_b, while the proof derives x_hat=(A+DeltaA)^dagger(b+delta_b).
ambiguities.evidence: The two formulations occur on the same page in Theorem 3.5 and its proof. The general backward-error definition requires x_hat to be an exact least-squares minimizer, which agrees with the pseudoinverse identity. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 906, equation (1.2); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5 and proof.)
ambiguities.impact: For an overdetermined problem, the literal equation is stronger and is not implied by the pseudoinverse identity unless b+delta_b lies in the range of A+DeltaA. A formalization must preserve this discrepancy or add an explicit range assumption rather than silently treating the two statements as equivalent.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase that z_hat satisfies the backward error does not specify that DeltaY_hat or delta_b is small.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.9) gives only the pseudoinverse witness relation. Smallness is introduced later as an additional O(u) condition in the interpretive paragraph. (PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, equation (3.9); PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, discussion following Theorem 3.5.)
ambiguities.impact: The formal implication holds for the supplied witnesses regardless of their size, but a claim of backward stability requires extra assumptions not contained in the theorem statement.

ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 1.3 draws a random sketch, but Theorem 3.5 does not identify a distribution or probability of satisfying its conditions.
ambiguities.evidence: Random drawing appears in step 1 of Algorithm 1.3, whereas Theorem 3.5 simply assumes that the realized S and A satisfy equations (3.6) and (3.7). (PDF p. 5, printed p. 909, Algorithm 1.3; PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5.)
ambiguities.impact: The theorem should be represented as a deterministic conditional result, not as a high-probability theorem, unless an additional embedding result is supplied.

ambiguities.issue: The relative right-hand-side criterion used in the explanatory O(u) statement has an unaddressed b=0 case.
ambiguities.evidence: The base problem permits arbitrary b in R^m, while the interpretation uses ||delta_b||_2/||b||_2 without stating b nonzero. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 905, equation (1.1); PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, following discussion.)
ambiguities.impact: This affects only the explanatory backward-stability criterion, not the formal perturbation relation or matrix bound.

ambiguities.issue: Exceptional floating-point behavior is not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: The numerical preliminaries state a precision-u rounding model and standard gamma bounds but do not mention overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, or infinities. (PDF p. 10, printed p. 914, section 2.3 and equation (2.1).)
ambiguities.impact: Such exclusions may be conventional in classical error analysis, but they are inherited conventions rather than explicit hypotheses of the selected theorem.

contract_plain_english: For a full-rank tall least-squares problem and a realized sketch satisfying the exact dimension, conditioning, and precision inequalities of Theorem 3.4, run SAA Blendenpik by explicitly forming Y_hat=A R_hat^(-1), applying unpreconditioned LSQR, and performing one final back substitution. If the terminal LSQR iterate admits z_hat=(Y_hat+DeltaY_hat)^dagger(b+delta_b), the proof composes the LSQR perturbation, the preconditioned-matrix formation error, and the final triangular-solve perturbation into the exact four-term DeltaA formula. It then proves ||DeltaA||_2<||S||_2||A||_2(6.04 n gamma_n||(S Q_A)^dagger||_2+2.01||DeltaY_hat||_2), with gamma_n=n u/(1-n u), without discarding the cross term DeltaY_hat DeltaR_hat. The theorem does not bound delta_b or DeltaY_hat, and overall O(u) backward stability is only a later conditional interpretation. The theorem text's literal perturbed equation and the proof's pseudoinverse least-squares identity are not equivalent for an inconsistent overdetermined problem and must be recorded as an unresolved discrepancy. (PDF p. 14, printed p. 918, equations (3.6)-(3.7); PDF p. 16, printed p. 920, Theorem 3.5 and proof; PDF p. 17, printed p. 921, completion and interpretation.)
